blockers.quote: if no living person knows where it is, within ten metres, a line draws itself from your shoes to it, with the distance
blockers.why: Check #3, Second hook by 0:30: the title promises anything ever lost, but the stated rule limits the power to ten metres. Later forty-metre, sea and kilometre uses silently discard that limit.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "if no living person knows where it is, a line draws itself from your shoes to it, with the distance; one line at a time."

blockers.quote: you whisper for the Konkan wreck again, then for every gold earring that ever went down a drain in this city, one grate after another, then for everything the sea has taken off this coast
blockers.why: Fails #6 Every use has a gap and No new power rule after halfway. The wreck repeats its previous result, while plural searches introduce a category-search power absent from the singular rule.
blockers.fix: Before midpoint, plant three singular, still-unsearched objects. Request them here one at a time, with each result contradicting the expected location. Keep one active line; build the planet image with paper-map inserts of the routes rather than plural searches.

suggestions.quote: The whole sea is on your line. Drop it, for one pill?
suggestions.fix: Owner suggestion: plant before 0:30 that voluntarily dropping a line makes that target unfindable to you forever. Then choosing the pill permanently sacrifices the wreck instead of merely pausing its line.

suggestions.quote: Therefore you go for what has no owner left: lost crypto.
suggestions.fix: Make this jump argue the under-question: the route enters ground that would have to be torn open, so you stop at the boundary. Finding it should create a reason to leave it lost, not only an access problem.

keep.quote: Knowing where was never the hard part
Some things stay lost. Keeps the peace.
